8	# feat: xRegistry-backed message listing and typed subscription scaffolding
9	
10	**Home repo:** `intropy-cli` (this repository). The plan also touches two sibling
11	repos: `intropy-registry` (the xRegistry server, at `~/dev/intropy/intropy-registry`)
12	and the Intropy template library (fetched by `internal/template`). Paths below are
13	relative to the repo each unit names.
14	
15	## Overview
16	
17	Intropy now has a read-only, xRegistry-compliant registry of CloudEvents message
18	definitions, their payload JSON Schemas, and the endpoints that produce and
19	consume them. This plan makes the CLI a first-class consumer of that registry in
20	two steps:
21	
22	1. **Read:** new commands to list messages in the registry and show, for one
23	   message, exactly how to subscribe to it (CloudEvents type, schema reference,
24	   pubsub/topic channel, envelope mode).
25	2. **Scaffold:** a typed way for a template parameter to say "this component
26	   subscribes to message X from the registry", resolved at `int create` time
27	   into the concrete wiring values (`topic`, `pubsub`, `contract`, CloudEvents
28	   type) that template skeletons and `sys create` assembly already consume.
29	
30	The registry is read-only by design (`capabilities` advertises
31	`entities.mutable: false`); the CLI is a pure consumer. No registry writes are
32	in scope.
33	
34	---
35	
36	## Problem Frame
37	
38	Today, wiring a new subscriber component is manual and unverified: a developer
39	must know the CloudEvents type, the Service Bus topic and Dapr pubsub component
40	name, and the C# contract type, and type them into template values by hand.
41	Nothing checks these against a source of truth, so drift between what a
42	component subscribes to and what producers actually publish is invisible until
43	runtime.
44	
45	The registry (`intropy-registry`) exists precisely to be that source of truth:
46	messagegroups/messages carry `envelopemetadata` (CloudEvents `type`, `source`),
47	`dataschemaxid` pointing at a versioned JSON Schema, and `protocol`; endpoints
48	carry `usage: [producer|subscriber]`, `channel: <pubsub>/<topic>`, and
49	`messagegroups` xid references. Everything a subscriber needs is already
50	resolvable over the conformant read-only API (`GET`, `?filter`, `?inline`,
51	`?doc`, `/export`).
52	
53	---
54	
55	## Requirements Trace
56	
57	- R1. A user can enumerate the messages in the registry from the CLI, in a
58	  table and as JSON.
59	- R2. A user can ask the CLI how to subscribe to one message and get a
60	  complete, correct answer: CloudEvents type, dataschema xid and format,
61	  pubsub component and topic, protocol and envelope mode.
62	- R3. A template can declare a parameter as a typed registry message
63	  reference; `int create` validates the reference against the registry and
64	  fails fast on unknown or malformed references.
65	- R4. At scaffold time the reference is resolved into the existing wiring
66	  values (`topic`, `pubsub`, plus a suggested `contract` and the CloudEvents
67	  type) so skeletons and `sys create` assembly work unchanged and offline.
68	- R5. The scaffold record (`.intropy/scaffold.json`) records both the resolved
69	  values and the message xid, so later commands can detect registry drift.
70	- R6. All new CLI surface follows the AGENTS.md writing and verb conventions
71	  (`list` enumerates, `show` prints one thing; stdout results, stderr status).
72	- R7. The registry remains spec-compliant; any registry-side change is
73	  optional, additive, and follows the xRegistry core/message/endpoint specs.
74	
75	---
76	
77	## Scope Boundaries
78	
79	- No mutation of the registry from the CLI — the registry is git-authored and
80	  read-only, and this plan does not change that.
81	- No contract code generation from JSON Schema (e.g. emitting C# records).
82	  The resolved `contract` value behaves exactly as it does today; generation
83	  is a deliberate follow-up.
84	- No changes to `sys create`/`sys update` assembly logic — the resolved wiring
85	  reuses the existing vocabulary verbatim.
86	- No drift-detection command (`int ... status` against the registry) in this
87	  plan; the recorded xid (R5) is the enabling groundwork only.
88	
89	### Deferred to Follow-Up Work
90	
91	- Contract codegen from `dataschemaxid` JSON Schema into a per-system
92	  `Contracts` project: separate plan; the largest open design space (naming,
93	  namespaces, generated-vs-handwritten boundaries).
94	- Registry-side ergonomics (per-messagegroup `channel`, or endpoint
95	  `?filter` over `messagegroups` xids): only if the client-side join in U2
96	  proves awkward at real registry sizes.
97	- A `diff`/`status`-style command comparing recorded xids against the live
98	  registry.
99	
100	---
101	
102	## Context & Research
103	
104	### Relevant Code and Patterns
105	
106	CLI (this repo):
107	
108	- `internal/registry/` — the **OCI** client for releases/templates. Name
109	  collision: the new client package must not be named `registry`. Use
110	  `internal/xregistry/`.
111	- `internal/template/wiring.go` — the wiring vocabulary (`KeyTopic`,
112	  `KeyContract`, `KeyPubsub`, `KeyAppID`) and the strict/lenient record
113	  readers (`RecordValue`, `SoftValue`). Resolved subscription values land
114	  here verbatim.
115	- `internal/template/manifest.go` — template manifest schema; `FieldSpec` is
116	  the prompter/CLI view of `spec.parameters.properties` and already carries
117	  prompt-only metadata (`Suggestions`) that never enters JSON Schema
118	  validation. The typed-reference annotation extends this seam.
119	- `internal/template/scaffold.go` — the scaffold record; additive fields do
120	  not require a `ScaffoldSchemaVersion` bump.
121	- `internal/template/scaffold_list.go`, `internal/system/blocks.go` — how
122	  recorded values feed workspace facts and system assembly
123	  (`parseTopicBlock` reads `topic`/`contract`/`pubsub`).
124	- `cmd/intropy/int_create.go`, `internal/template/create.go`,
125	  `internal/template/prepare.go`, `internal/template/prompt.go`,
126	  `internal/template/suggest.go` — the create pipeline: value resolution,
127	  prompting, suggestion sources, render.
128	- `internal/config/` — per-context config resolution (pattern for adding the
129	  registry base URL).
130	- `cmd/intropy/release_list.go`, `cmd/intropy/release_show.go` — command
131	  shape, output/JSON handling, and error style to mirror.
132	
133	Registry (`~/dev/intropy/intropy-registry`):
134	
135	- Read-only conformant API: `GET /messagegroups/{gid}/messages/{mid}`,
136	  `?filter` (all operators), `?inline` (nested paths, `*`), `?doc`, `/export`
137	  (byte-identical to `/?doc&inline=*,capabilities,modelsource`), `/model`,
138	  `/capabilities`. Write verbs return 405.
139	- Content negotiation (`src/http/negotiate.ts`): HTML wins only when
140	  `text/html` is specifically acceptable and beats wildcards. Go's
141	  `http.Client` sends no `Accept` header when unset (which the negotiator
142	  treats as JSON-safe), **but the CLI sends `Accept: application/json`
143	  explicitly** so intent is unambiguous and future portal routes cannot
144	  surprise it.
145	- Naming conventions (README): `messageid` is the full CloudEvents `type`;
146	  `channel` on endpoints is `<pubsub>/<topic>` — exactly the CLI's `pubsub`
147	  and `topic` wiring values joined by `/`.
148	- Message → channel join: endpoints reference messagegroups via xids;
149	  `usage: [producer]` + `messagegroups: [/messagegroups/<gid>]` identifies
150	  the producing endpoint, whose `channel` gives pubsub/topic.
151	
152	### Institutional Learnings
153	
154	- AGENTS.md (this repo) is the binding style contract for all new CLI
155	  surface: command verbs (`list`/`show` are the read-only verbs; new nouns
156	  hang under `int` like `sys`, `template`, `release`), flag description
157	  constants in `cmd/intropy/flagtext.go`, lowercase no-period status lines
158	  on stderr, front-loaded errors with remediation on a second line.
159	
160	### External References
161	
162	- xRegistry core spec and CloudEvents message/endpoint registry models —
163	  vendored copies live in `intropy-registry/spec/` (`core-model.schema.json`,
164	  `message-model.json`, `endpoint-model.json`) and are the authority for any
165	  registry-side change.
166	
167	---
168	
169	## Key Technical Decisions
170	
171	- **New noun `message`, not `registry`:** the CLI's "registry" already means
172	  the OCI release/template registry (`internal/registry`, `release`
173	  commands). Overloading it for xRegistry would be actively misleading.
174	  Commands: `int message list`, `int message show <messageid>`.
175	- **`/export` + client-side join, not N+1 queries:** the registry is small
176	  and git-backed; one `GET /export` yields messagegroups, messages, schemas,
177	  and endpoints in a single document, and `show` joins locally. This avoids
178	  encoding registry-size assumptions into the client and needs no
179	  registry-side changes. Revisit if the registry grows.
180	- **Typed reference is a manifest annotation, not a new value type in
181	  templates:** `spec.parameters.properties.<name>` gains an optional
182	  extension key (e.g. `x-intropy-message-ref: true`, or a `format` the CLI
183	  recognizes). Templates still render plain strings; the CLI resolves the
184	  reference into the existing wiring values before render. This keeps the
185	  template surface unchanged and makes resolution testable in the CLI alone.
186	- **Resolution happens once, at create time, and is recorded:** the scaffold
187	  record gains an additive field (e.g. `subscriptions: [{message: "<xid>",
188	  schemaVersion: "1"}]`) alongside the resolved `topic`/`pubsub`/`contract`
189	  values. Offline `sys create` and suggestions keep working from the resolved
190	  values; the xid enables future drift checks. No `ScaffoldSchemaVersion`
191	  bump (additive).
192	- **Channel ownership:** the producing endpoint's `channel`
193	  (`<pubsub>/<topic>`) is the source of truth for where to subscribe. If no
194	  producer endpoint exists for a messagegroup, `message show` reports the
195	  message fully and says the channel is not declared (a registry authoring
196	  gap, not a CLI error); scaffolding refuses the reference with a
197	  remediation line.
198	- **`contract` stays developer-owned, with a registry-derived suggestion:**
199	  the registry's `schemaid` (e.g. `product-export.v1`) is a kebab-case
200	  document id, not a C# type name, and no generated type exists until the
201	  deferred codegen follow-up. Deriving `contract` silently would record a
202	  type that exists nowhere. So the resolver *suggests* a contract name —
203	  strip the `.vN` suffix, kebab→Pascal (`product-export.v1` →
204	  `ProductExport`) — and the developer confirms or overrides it at the
205	  prompt (or via `--set contract=`). The schema xid and version recorded in
206	  `subscriptions` keep the provenance that a future codegen pass or drift
207	  check reconciles against. Collision handling for the suggestion (two
208	  schemaids mapping to one Pascal name) is a prompt-time concern only: the
209	  developer's confirmed value is what gets recorded.
210	- **Bare message ids must be unambiguous:** `message show <messageid>` and
211	  message-ref parameters accept a bare messageid; nothing in the registry
212	  prevents the same CloudEvents type in two messagegroups. A bare id that
213	  matches more than one message is an error listing the matching xids; the
214	  full xid form always resolves exactly.
215	- **Recorded schema version comes from the schema resource's default
216	  version:** `dataschemaxid` points at the schema resource (no
217	  `/versions/<id>` suffix), so the resolver reads the schema's default
218	  version id from the export document and records that in `subscriptions`.
219	
220	---
221	
222	## Open Questions
223	
224	### Resolved During Planning
225	
226	- Does the registry API suffice as-is? Yes — `/export`, `?doc`, and the
227	  endpoint `channel` convention cover list, show, and resolution without
228	  registry changes.
229	- Where does the registry base URL live? Resolved through the existing
230	  `config.Resolve` precedence — `--registry-url` flag > `INTROPY_REGISTRY_URL`
231	  env var > customer context in the config file — matching every sibling
232	  setting (`INTROPY_GITOPS_REPO`, `INTROPY_TEMPLATE_REPO`). New shared flag
233	  constant in `cmd/intropy/flagtext.go`. The config key must exist before
234	  users can set it: `config.Load` uses `KnownFields(true)`, so an unknown
235	  key in the config file is a load error.
236	- How is `contract` derived from the registry? It isn't — it stays
237	  developer-owned with a registry-derived suggestion (see Key Technical
238	  Decisions). Silent derivation would record a C# type that exists nowhere
239	  until the codegen follow-up.
240	- Must the CLI handle registry unavailability during `int create`? Yes:
241	  non-registry templates are unaffected; a template *with* a message-ref
242	  parameter fails fast with a front-loaded error naming the registry and the
243	  unreachable URL.
244	
245	### Deferred to Implementation
246	
247	- Exact extension-key name and shape in the template manifest
248	  (`x-intropy-message-ref` boolean vs. a structured object): settle against
249	  the real template library during U4.
250	- Whether `message show` renders the schema document inline (via `?doc`) or
251	  only its xid/version: decide against actual output readability.
252	- How multiple producer endpoints for one messagegroup are surfaced (list
253	  all channels vs. error): depends on whether the registry ever has more
254	  than one.
255	
256	---
257	
258	## High-Level Technical Design
259	
260	> *This illustrates the intended approach and is directional guidance for
261	> review, not implementation specification. The implementing agent should
262	> treat it as context, not code to reproduce.*
263	
264	```mermaid
265	flowchart LR
266	    subgraph CLI
267	      MC[int message list/show] --> XR[internal/xregistry client]
268	      CR[int create] --> RES[message-ref resolver]
269	      RES --> XR
270	      RES --> SC[.intropy/scaffold.json\nvalues + subscriptions]
271	    end
272	    XR -->|GET /export, /messagegroups/... Accept: application/json| REG[(intropy-registry\nread-only xRegistry API)]
273	    SC --> SYS[sys create assembly\nexisting wiring vocabulary]
274	    SC --> SKEL[template skeletons\nplain string values]
275	```
276	
277	Resolution data flow (create time, per message-ref parameter):
278	
279	1. Prompt/flag yields a message reference (`<messageid>` or full xid
280	   `/messagegroups/<gid>/messages/<mid>`).
281	2. Resolver fetches `/export` (cached per create run) and locates the
282	   message; unknown id → usage error listing close matches.
283	3. Resolver finds the producer endpoint for the message's group and splits
284	   `channel` into `pubsub` + `topic`.
285	4. Resolver derives the CloudEvents `type` from `envelopemetadata`, reads
286	   the schema resource at `dataschemaxid` for its id and default version,
287	   and builds the suggested `contract` name (strip `.vN`, kebab→Pascal).
288	5. Values map gains `topic` and `pubsub`, the `contract` suggestion feeds
289	   the prompt (developer confirms or overrides), and the recorded
290	   `subscriptions` entry carries the message xid, schemaid and versionid;
291	   render proceeds exactly as today.
292	
293	---
294	
295	## Implementation Units
296	
297	- [x] U1. **xRegistry client package (`internal/xregistry`)**
298	
299	**Goal:** A typed, testable read-only client for the registry — fetch the
300	export document and individual entities, with models for messagegroups,
301	messages, schemas, and endpoints — plus the config plumbing that gives it a
302	base URL.
303	
304	**Requirements:** R1, R2, R7
305	
306	**Dependencies:** None
307	
308	**Files:**
309	- Create: `internal/xregistry/client.go`
310	- Create: `internal/xregistry/types.go`
311	- Modify: `internal/config/` (registry URL in the resolved config,
312	  following the flag > env > context > file precedence; the config key

316	**Approach:**
317	- One constructor taking base URL + `http.Client`; every request sends
318	  `Accept: application/json` (explicit intent; the negotiator also treats
319	  an absent or wildcard-only Accept as JSON, but the explicit header is
320	  the contract).
321	- Config plumbing lands here, not in the commands: both U2 and U4 need
322	  the resolved URL, so the config key, env var (`INTROPY_REGISTRY_URL`)
323	  and `config.Resolve` wiring are prerequisites of anything registry-aware.
324	- `Export(ctx)` fetches `GET /export`; entity getters (`Message`,
325	  `ProducerEndpointFor`) operate on the exported document so one fetch
326	  serves a whole command or create run.
327	- Errors wrap with context per AGENTS.md (`get export: ...`); 404/non-2xx
328	  and JSON parse failures are distinct, front-loaded errors.
329	- Mirror the structure and test style of `internal/registry/` (OCI client)
330	  without sharing code — the two registries are unrelated domains.

340	  export document
341	- Edge case: message id that exists in a group but with no producer endpoint
342	  → `ProducerEndpointFor` reports "no producer" distinctly from "not found"
343	- Edge case: base URL with trailing slash → requests are well-formed
344	- Error path: server returns 500 → error names the operation and status
345	- Error path: server returns invalid JSON → parse error naming the path
346	- Error path: unknown message id → not-found error carrying the id

349	- Package builds and tests pass; a real `GET /export` against

355	- [x] U2. **`int message list` and `int message show` commands**
356	
357	**Goal:** Read-only commands answering "what messages exist" and "how do I
358	subscribe to this one".
359	
360	**Requirements:** R1, R2, R6
361

=== README ===
# intropy-registry

A narrow, [xRegistry](https://xregistry.io)-compliant registry for CloudEvents
definitions, their payload schemas, and the endpoints that produce and consume
them.

Standards-compliant, deliberately small. It borrows EventCatalog's git-as-source-of-truth
authoring model and its look, but not its surface area — there are no domains,
flows, ADRs, teams, ownership, changelog, AI agents or generators.

## Why

Intropy has no contract governance. Message contracts are plain C# `record` types
in a per-System `Contracts` project, shared by `ProjectReference`, so cross-team
and cross-repo contract evolution is unguarded. No JSON Schema, Avro or Protobuf
exists for any business payload, and the CloudEvents `dataschema` attribute is
never set and never read.

This gives you a resolvable `dataschema` URI, a reviewable diff when a contract
changes, and one readable page per event.

## Shape

Git-first and **read-only**. Definitions are authored as files under `registry/`
and reviewed in a PR; the server exposes them over a conformant read-only
xRegistry API. The core spec explicitly provides for this — `/capabilities`
advertises `available.entities.mutable: false`, and every write verb returns 405.

Three group types, from the CloudEvents Registry:

| Group | Resource | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `messagegroups` | `messages` | `hasdocument: false`, `maxversions: 1` — pure metadata |
| `schemagroups` | `schemas` | documents, versions, format and compatibility validation |
| `endpoints` | *(imports `messages`)* | producers and consumers, referencing messagegroups |

Narrowed to `CloudEvents/1.0` envelopes, `JsonSchema/draft/2020-12` payloads and
the `AMQP/1.0` and `HTTP` protocols Intropy actually deploys. The narrowing is one
object — `NARROWING` in `src/registry/model.ts` — and widening it is an edit there
and nowhere else.

## Authoring

```
registry/
  registry.yaml                                  registryid, name, baseurl
  messagegroups/<messagegroupid>.yaml            the group and its messages
  schemagroups/<schemagroupid>/
    group.yaml
    <schemaid>/
      schema.yaml                                format, compatibility, default version
      1.json                                     version documents, named by versionid
  endpoints/<endpointid>.yaml
```

`createdat` / `modifiedat` fall back to file mtime, and `epoch` defaults to 1.
Set them explicitly for reproducible builds — a git-backed registry has no natural
epoch counter.

### Naming

| id | Rule | Example |
|---|---|---|
| `messagegroupid` | `<reverse-domain>.<customer>.<domain>` | `io.intropy.maxbo.product` |
| `messageid` | the full CloudEvents `type` | `io.intropy.maxbo.product.export` |

A breaking change means a **new schema resource**, not a new version — hence the
major version in `schemaid`. That is why versions can be validated for
compatibility at all.

Non-conforming event types are a **warning**, never an error. The extractor
template currently generates a non-reverse-DNS form, so rejecting would make the
registry unable to hold events that already exist in production. More broadly:
an invalid entity is dropped with an error, an unresolved reference is kept with
a warning. A registry mid-edit is still worth serving.

## Running

[go-task](https://taskfile.dev) is the front door; the npm scripts underneath still work.

```
task                # list everything
task dev            # the real thing on :8787 — API, portal and negotiation
task dev:site       # astro on :4321 with HMR — fast UI work, no negotiation or API
task verify         # the full gate: typecheck, tests, build, live conformance
```

Driving it from an agent or a script:

```
task dev:bg         # start in the background, wait until it answers
task dev:status
task dev:logs
task dev:stop
```

`task verify` starts a server, runs the 54 spec assertions against it, and stops
it again — including when the assertions fail, so a red run never leaves a stray
process holding the port.

The Worker rehydrates the built tree at cold start and serializes per request,
so a plain GET and a `?filter`'d GET come from the same code path and cannot drift.

## Portal and API on one URL

xRegistry puts the registry root at `/`, and a portal wants a page there too. One
path can only be one thing, so the two share every path and are separated by
`Accept`:

```bash
curl        localhost:8787/                      # JSON — the registry root
curl -H 'Accept: text/html' localhost:8787/      # HTML — the portal
open        http://localhost:8787/               # HTML
```

The rule (`src/http/negotiate.ts`) is that HTML wins only when `text/html` is
acceptable *specifically* and at least as strongly as `application/json`, and more
strongly than any wildcard. A wildcard alone is never enough — **curl sends `*/*`
and must keep getting JSON**. Every response carries `Vary: Accept` so a cache
cannot serve one to the other.

Two deliberate exceptions:

- `/model`, `/capabilities` and `/export` are API-only. They have no page, so a
  browser gets JSON.
- An API path with no portal page yet **falls back to JSON** rather than 404ing.
  The resource does exist; only the page is missing. Phase 2 fills these in.

`run_worker_first = true` in `wrangler.toml` is load-bearing. Without it
Cloudflare's asset router serves `dist/site/index.html` for `/` before the Worker
ever runs, and every API client gets the portal instead of the registry root.
Unit tests cannot catch this — they call the Worker directly — so it is asserted
in `scripts/conformance.sh` against a real server.

## Compliance

Implemented: `GET` on every entity path, `/model`, `/capabilities`, `/export`,
`?filter` (all operators, AND within a parameter, OR across parameters), `?inline`
(nested paths, `*`, relative to the entity retrieved), `?doc` / `?nodoc`,
`Link: rel=xregistry-root`, and 405 on every write.

`GET /export` is byte-identical to `GET /?doc&inline=*,capabilities,modelsource`,
which is asserted in both the test suite and the conformance script.

Not implemented, and not advertised: mutation, pagination, auth.

`formatvalidated` is earned, not asserted — every schema document is compiled with
ajv at build time and the flag is set from the result.

### Two upstream notes

**The published meta-schema rejects the published schema model.**
`spec/schema/model.json` uses `validateformat`, `validatecompatibility` and
`strictvalidation`, all documented in `core/model.md`, but
`core/model.schema.json` forbids them via `additionalProperties: false`. We keep
the keys — `validateformat: true` is what makes `formatvalidated` mean anything —
and `tests/model.test.ts` asserts our flattening adds no violations beyond those
three. If upstream fixes the meta-schema, the allowlist empties and the test
tightens on its own.

**The vendored meta-schema declares `https://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema#`**,
while ajv registers draft-07 under `http://`. The test registers the alias.

## Status

Phases 1 and 2 are complete: the read-only API, content negotiation, and the
portal — overview, events catalog with filtering, event pages, schema pages with
version diffs, and endpoint pages, on the Manual light surface.

Portal routes mirror the xRegistry paths, so `/messagegroups/<g>/messages/<m>` is
both the API resource and the page. `/events` is the one portal-only route: a flat
catalog the API has no equivalent for.

All four phases are complete: the read-only API, content negotiation, the portal,
the topology graph, a `⌘K` command palette, and the accessibility and caching
pass. Lighthouse is 100 for accessibility, best practices and SEO on every page
type.

Portal-only routes: `/events`, `/graph`, `/api`. Everything else mirrors an
xRegistry path.

A real schema (from ~/dev/intropy/intropy-registry/registry/schemagroups/io.intropy.maxbo.product/product-export.v1/2.json) uses: draft 2020-12, `title`, `description`, `type: object`, `additionalProperties: false`, `required[]`, `properties` with `type: string|integer|array`, `format: date-time`, `enum` of kebab-case strings, `items.$ref: "#/$defs/ExportEventFile"`, and a `$defs` map of nested object schemas. The generated types must land in the **shared-contracts** sibling project. 1. **The generator package.** Where it lives, its exported API (input: schema document + root type name + namespace; output: file content(s)), and its internal model. It must be independently unit-testable with schema fixtures and no network.

2. **The type mapping**, as a decided table: object→record, array→IReadOnlyList<T>, $ref/$defs→named nested types, string/integer/number/boolean, `format` (date-time, date, uuid, …), nullable unions `["string","null"]`, enums of kebab strings, required vs optional. resolution has outrun the scaffold it feeds:

1. **The resolved pubsub never reaches the generated code.**

   accepts any event on its topic — though the registry documents `source` as
   existing "for echo prevention".
2. **The payload schema is fetched and thrown away.**
   `xregistry.SchemaVersion.Document` already holds the inlined JSON Schema;
   nothing reads it. Meanwhile `shared-contracts` renders
   `public record ProductExport();` and the scaffolded loader integration test
   admits in a comment that it "deliberately uses its own field names instead
   of guessing the eventual shape".
3. **`subscriptions[]` is write-only.** Nothing reads it back — not even
   `int show`, whose `formatScaffold` never prints it. The dashboard still
   ships a `PLACEHOLDER_SCHEMA` in `ContractDetail.tsx` because .NET hosts do
   not emit `contracts[].schema`.

Outcome: picking a message becomes the single act that wires a subscriber —
routing, envelope identity and the payload type all follow from it — and the
record stays readable enough afterwards to tell when the registry has moved on.

---

## Design decisions

**D1. The CLI flattens the schema; the template renders the C#.**
`internal/template/reserved.go` exists for exactly this case: *"spec.parameters
is scalar-only by design, so a skeleton cannot declare 'the list of ports' as a
parameter. These keys are how it gets one anyway: the caller injects the
structures after validation, and the skeleton ranges over them. Which files a
render produces is then decided by a spec.files condition over the same data."*
So a new reserved key carries a flattened field tree and the shared-contracts
skeleton ranges over it. All C# text stays in `intropy-templates`, versioned
with the template release; the CLI stays a schema flattener. Regeneration then
comes free — it is just a re-render, so `RenderUpdate` applies unchanged.

**D2. `spec.files` selects between the two shapes of the contract file.**
Today `{{ .contract }}.cs.tmpl` declares a primary constructor, and two records
cannot both do so. `FileRule{Path, When}` is matched against the *source* path
with sprig available (`internal/template/render.go:32`), so:

| source path | `when` |
|---|---|
| `Generated/{{ .contract }}.g.cs.tmpl` | shape present |
| `{{ .contract }}Rules.cs.tmpl` | shape present |
| `{{ .contract }}.cs.tmpl` | shape absent (today's sample/empty shell, untouched) |
| `OrderLine.cs.tmpl` | shape absent **and** `not .empty` (currently just the latter) |

The `.g.cs` holds `public partial record X(...)`; `XRules.cs` is the
parameterless `partial record X { }` companion for hand-written members.

**D3. The type mapping is CLI-owned and resolved in the flattener's output**,
so the template does no mapping. Decided table: object → nested record named
from its `$defs` key; array → `IReadOnlyList<T>`; string → `string` with
`format` date-time → `DateTimeOffset`, date → `DateOnly`, time → `TimeOnly`,
uuid → `Guid`, anything else → `string`; integer → `int` (`format: int64` →
`long`); number → `decimal`; boolean → `bool`; `["X","null"]` or absent from
`required` → `T?`. A string `enum` becomes `string` plus a
`static class <Prop>Values` of consts and an XML doc listing them — **not** a
C# enum: the registry's values are kebab-case (`product-attribute`), a real
enum needs a converter plus member-name mapping, and the schema is the
contract. `Contracts.csproj` is SDK-style with `Nullable` and `ImplicitUsings`
enabled, so `IReadOnlyList<>`/`DateTimeOffset` need no usings, nullable
annotations are meaningful, and `Generated/*.g.cs` is globbed in automatically.

**D4. Property order is preserved explicitly.** `json.Unmarshal` into a Go map
loses `properties` declaration order, and C# positional records require
optional parameters last. The flattener walks `properties` with a
`json.Decoder` token stream to keep order, then emits required members in
declaration order followed by optional ones in declaration order, each with
`= null`. Deterministic, and it compiles.

**D5. Unsupported constructs become Gaps, never guesses.** For `oneOf`,
`allOf`, `anyOf`, `patternProperties`, tuple-form `items`, a `$ref` outside
`#/$defs`, or recursion past a depth cap: the member's type becomes
`JsonElement`, the generated file carries a `// gap:` comment naming the
construct, and the flattener returns `[]Gap` that the create flow prints to
stderr. This is the house rule (borrow what reliably works, surface the rest as
Gaps) and it beats emitting a confidently wrong type.

**D6. The registry owns routing and envelope identity; the developer owns the
contract *name*.** `injectWiringValue` already encodes exactly this three-way
authority rule for `topic`/`pubsub` (identical accepted, conflicting `--set` an
error, any other layer yields with a stderr note). `eventType`/`eventSource`
join it. `contract` stays as it is — the registry supplies the *shape*, not the
type name.

**D7. `intropy int update` is the regeneration verb.** AGENTS.md:141 defines
`update` as *"reconciles something installed against the ref its source now
pins… It never changes which ref is pinned"*, and `int` has no `update` yet
(only create/describe/list/local/show). Which *message* a component subscribes
to is the developer's pin and stays untouched; the schema *version* is the
registry publisher's, so adopting it is reconciling, not re-pinning.
`RenderUpdate`'s `Baseline` is the shape re-flattened from the **recorded**
`SchemaVersion` — the export carries every version under `Schema.Versions`, so
the baseline is derivable — which makes an untouched `.g.cs` report `updated`
and a hand-edited one `conflict`. A recorded version the registry has since
dropped leaves `baselineKnown` false and everything differing conflicts, the
conservative fallback `render.go` already documents.

**D8. A reused shared-contracts project gets the generated subtree added.**
`internal/template/dependencies.go:97` skips a reused dependency entirely, so a
second component's contract would land nowhere. On reuse, when a shape is
present, render only the `Generated/**` and `<Contract>Rules.cs` rules through
`RenderUpdate` into the existing project.

parameter annotated `x-intropy-message-ref: true` holds an xRegistry message
id, and `int create` resolves it against one `GET /export` into `topic` +
`pubsub` values, a suggested `contract` name, and a `SubscriptionRecord` in
`.intropy/scaffold.json`. The CLI prompt, the dashboard drawer and
`int message list/show` all work.

resolution has outrun the scaffold it feeds:

1. **The resolved pubsub never reaches the generated code.**
   `loader/skeleton/src/Constants.cs.tmpl` and
   `extractor/skeleton/src/Constants.cs.tmpl` hardcode
   `PubSubName = "pubsub"`, while `sys create`'s `Topics.cs.tmpl` correctly
   renders `TopicRef<T>.Define("{{ $t.pubsub }}", …)` from the record. Pick
   `io.intropy.maxbo.product.export` today and the host declares the topic on
   `product-distribution-pubsub` while the component subscribes on `pubsub`.
   The CloudEvents `type` and `source` reach no skeleton at all, so a loader
   accepts any event on its topic — though the registry documents `source` as
   existing "for echo prevention".
2. **The payload schema is fetched and thrown away.**
   `xregistry.SchemaVersion.Document` already holds the inlined JSON Schema;
   nothing reads it. Meanwhile `shared-contracts` renders
   `public record ProductExport();` and the scaffolded loader integration test
   admits in a comment that it "deliberately uses its own field names instead
   of guessing the eventual shape".
3. **`subscriptions[]` is write-only.** Nothing reads it back — not even
   `int show`, whose `formatScaffold` never prints it. The dashboard still
   ships a `PLACEHOLDER_SCHEMA` in `ContractDetail.tsx` because .NET hosts do
   not emit `contracts[].schema`.

routing, envelope identity and the payload type all follow from it — and the
record stays readable enough afterwards to tell when the registry has moved on.

---

## Design decisions

**D1. The CLI flattens the schema; the template renders the C#.**
`internal/template/reserved.go` exists for exactly this case: *"spec.parameters
is scalar-only by design, so a skeleton cannot declare 'the list of ports' as a
parameter. These keys are how it gets one anyway: the caller injects the
structures after validation, and the skeleton ranges over them. Which files a
render produces is then decided by a spec.files condition over the same data."*

skeleton ranges over it. All C# text stays in `intropy-templates`, versioned
with the template release; the CLI stays a schema flattener. Regeneration then
comes free — it is just a re-render, so `RenderUpdate` applies unchanged.

**D2. `spec.files` selects between the two shapes of the contract file.**
Today `{{ .contract }}.cs.tmpl` declares a primary constructor, and two records
cannot both do so. `FileRule{Path, When}` is matched against the *source* path
with sprig available (`internal/template/render.go:32`), so:

| source path | `when` |
|---|---|
| `Generated/{{ .contract }}.g.cs.tmpl` | shape present |
| `{{ .contract }}Rules.cs.tmpl` | shape present |
| `{{ .contract }}.cs.tmpl` | shape absent (today's sample/empty shell, untouched) |
| `OrderLine.cs.tmpl` | shape absent **and** `not .empty` (currently just the latter) |

parameterless `partial record X { }` companion for hand-written members.

so the template does no mapping. Decided table: object → nested record named
from its `$defs` key; array → `IReadOnlyList<T>`; string → `string` with
`format` date-time → `DateTimeOffset`, date → `DateOnly`, time → `TimeOnly`,
uuid → `Guid`, anything else → `string`; integer → `int` (`format: int64` →
`long`); number → `decimal`; boolean → `bool`; `["X","null"]` or absent from

`static class <Prop>Values` of consts and an XML doc listing them — **not** a

enum needs a converter plus member-name mapping, and the schema is the
contract. `Contracts.csproj` is SDK-style with `Nullable` and `ImplicitUsings`
